cases.customer_question: Can a Bluetooth product still be qualified when the selected QDID combination produces Consistency Check / IDL errors that require unsupported ICS modifications from the chip vendor?
question_variants: Can qualification proceed with Consistency Check errors?
What happens if IDL errors remain in a QDID combination?
Can PRD2.3 QDIDs still be used despite ICS inconsistencies?
Can we qualify a product if the IC vendor no longer supports ICS updates?
Are unresolved inter-layer dependency errors always fatal?
cases.actual_issue: Determining whether a Bluetooth SIG qualification can proceed when a reused QDID combination triggers inter-layer dependency (IDL) consistency check errors and the original silicon vendor no longer supports ICS corrections.
cases.plain_english_explanation: Bluetooth qualification tools check whether all Bluetooth layers and features are logically compatible. Sometimes older QDID combinations produce consistency check errors because the feature definitions no longer align with newer qualification rules. In some limited cases, older PRD2.3-based registrations can still be reused if specific qualification conditions are met.
cases.consultant_answer: The consultant confirmed that the referenced QDID combination generated multiple GAP and LL inter-layer dependency inconsistencies during the Consistency Check. The consultant explained that another certification body had identified the need for ICS modifications from the IC vendor, but the vendor no longer supported the old device. Despite the remaining IDL errors, the consultant stated that the customer's requested registration could still proceed because the reused PRD2.3 QDID combination satisfied specific conditions allowing new registration even with unresolved Consistency Check errors.
cases.decision_logic: Not all IDL or Consistency Check errors automatically block qualification. Certain legacy PRD2.3 QDID reuse scenarios may remain acceptable if the qualification conditions permit reuse without requiring unsupported ICS modifications.
cases.final_recommendation: Evaluate whether the QDID reuse scenario qualifies under legacy PRD2.3 reuse conditions before attempting ICS modification work. If the chip vendor no longer supports the platform, confirm whether the remaining IDL errors are acceptable under the applicable qualification path.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Assuming all IDL errors are fatal may cause unnecessary redesign work or migration to newer silicon. Conversely, ignoring non-permitted IDL inconsistencies could lead to rejected qualification submissions.
